rows.text: Charged $14.99 to Morgan's card, paid to Nomiq Domains.
rows.quote: Renewed halcyonthreshold.org for one year ($14.99 on the Visa ending 4417; it now runs to 19 Nov 2027).

rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Priya Raman <priya.raman@fastmail.com> with subject "Re: Offer of help". It read: "Hi Priya, Thank you, and sorry for the slow reply. A concrete offer of five hours a week is exactly what a project this size needs. Here's what I'm leaning toward. Proposed rules for frontier-AI incident reporting (e.g. docket FMIR-2026-0042) depend heavily on how \"serious safety incident\" is defined. I'd like to build a small open dataset of publicly documented AI incidents and near-misses, each coded as reportable / not reportable / ambiguous under the draft definition, with some double-coding to measure where reasonable readers disagree. Then I'd write up the main ambiguities. A good first piece for you, if it appeals: spend a couple of hours checking whether anyone has already done this (the AI Incident Database, OECD's AI incident monitor, academic papers mapping incidents to regulatory definitions). If someone has, I'd rather help them than duplicate them. After that, sourcing and coding incidents, plus the inter-coder agreement analysis, would be squarely your skills. No pressure if that's not the kind of thing you had in mind. Tell me what you'd enjoy and we'll find a fit. Best, Morgan"
rows.quote: Replied to Priya, offering her that first check as a starting task and then the data work on the project.

rows.text: Created a recurring schedule named "Halcyon weekly triage" (0 8 * * 1) that starts new sessions of the agent.
rows.quote: Set up a weekly check-in every Monday at 8am. It sorts Halcyon email and moves the project forward
